title: Coming out hoop in cross-stitch
subtitle: "Out and proud" in a rainbow arc above a small heart
excerpt: A coming-out hoop stitches the phrase "out and proud" in a curved rainbow arc on 14-count Aida. The six classic rainbow colours (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet) each cover one or two letters of the phrase, and a small rainbow heart sits below. The piece is about 80-by-70 stitches and finishes at about 14 x 13 cm in a 15 cm hoop.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library.

content.text: A coming-out hoop stitches the phrase "out and proud" across an 80-by-70 stitch piece on 14-count

. The letters run in a gentle arc across the upper half, each coloured in one of the six classic rainbow stripes. A small rainbow heart, horizontal stripes within a heart silhouette, sits centred below the text. Eleven
colours cover the piece. The curved letter placement is what makes this INTERMEDIATE: the letters are offset by one or two rows at each end of the arc, which requires careful chart-reading.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white
items.substitutions: White is strongly recommended here, rainbow colours need a neutral background

items.name: DMC floss for text outlines (optional)
items.qty: 1 skein blanc for back-stitch outlining between letters if colours run together

content.text: Find the fabric centre. The chart centre falls on the A of "AND" in the phrase. Begin there and work outward, placing each letter in its correct row offset for the arc shape.

Stitch each letter completely before moving to the next. The arc offset means the letters at the ends of the phrase sit 3 or 4 rows lower than the central letters. Count carefully from the chart baseline for each letter.
Colour assignment: the six colours split across the twelve letters and spaces. Follow the chart key, the colour boundary typically falls mid-word rather than at word breaks.
Stitch the rainbow heart below the text once all letters are complete. The heart uses the same six stripe colours in horizontal bands within the heart silhouette.
Wash gently and press face-down. Display in the hoop as finished art, the round hoop suits the arc composition better than a rectangular frame.

items.symptom: The rainbow arc colours overlap at the edges
items.cause: Each arc colour was stitched beyond its boundary before the adjacent colour was placed.
items.fix: Work each arc colour to the exact boundary shown on the chart before starting the next. A shared boundary line means the last column of one colour and the first column of the next share no squares. Once both boundary columns are in, the colours should meet cleanly.

items.symptom: The text looks uneven within the arc
items.cause: The lettering was positioned by eye rather than from the counted centre of the arc.
items.fix: Count the total stitch width of the text first, then find the arc centre and work outward. Place the centre letter before stitching any others. The text should read level once each letter's base row aligns with the arc centreline.

content.text: The all-are-welcome sampler in this sub-category is a larger piece. It has a full border, a more complex layout, and several motifs. It is a big step up from this hoop.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
